title: Restricted Fourier coefficient estimation error
statement: Let $n>0$, and let $\varepsilon=a/b$ be specified by positive integers $a,b$ with $2a\le b$. Let $s\ge1$ be an integer, and let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ have Fourier $1$-norm at most $s$. For any coordinate set $J$, any subset $S$ of its indices, and any fixed sign assignment $z$ on the complementary coordinates, the absolute difference between the restricted Fourier coefficient estimate for $f$ at $(J,S,z)$ and the corresponding restricted Fourier coefficient is at most $\varepsilon/4$.
hypotheses_covered: The Fourier bound $s$ is an integer with $s\ge1$
The target is a sign-valued function on $\{−1,1\}^n$
$J$ is a subset of the coordinate indices
$z$ is a sign assignment on the complementary coordinates
